claims.text: The Bureau of Experts record names the instrument as Royal Order A/91 of 27/8/1412 AH and prints the issue date 1412/08/27 AH, equal to 01/03/1992, and the publication date 1412/09/02 AH, equal to 06/03/1992. It marks the law as in force (ساري).
claims.locator: Law summary panel (تاريخ الإصدار، تاريخ النشر، الحالة، أدوات إصدار النظام)
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only: a statute record that dates the law, not any Chairman, and is never a holder date. The Bureau's English translation cover prints March 2, 1992 (sa_shura_law_en_cover_19920302), one day later; the Royal Embassy's release of 5 July 1997 dates A/90 and A/91 of 27/8/1412 H to March 1, 1992 (sa_shura_membership_90_a63_19970705), agreeing with this record. claims.text: The order's clauses issue the law in the attached form; replace the Shura Council law of 1347 AH and provide that the Council's arrangements are settled by royal order; keep existing laws in force until amended; apply the law within at most six months of its publication; and publish it in the official gazette.
claims.locator: Royal Order A/91, clauses First to Fifth
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. It sets no date of formation and names no Chairman.

claims.text: The original Article 3 provides for a Chairman and sixty members chosen by the King. The record's amendment notes cite Royal Order A/26 of 1426/3/2 AH (a Chairman and 150 members) and A/44 of 1434/2/29 AH (women at least 20 per cent).
claims.locator: Article 3 and its amendment notes
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. The captured notes do not list the 1418 AH and 1422 AH changes to 90 and 120 members that other sources cite (A/62 or A/63 of 1418 AH; A/78 of 1/3/1422 AH).

claims.text: Article 10: the Chairman of the Shura Council, his deputy and the Secretary-General are appointed and relieved by royal orders, which also set their ranks, rights, duties and affairs. An amendment by Royal Order A/181 of 14/12/1428 AH adds the Assistant Chairman.
claims.locator: Article 10 and its amendment note
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. The chair therefore begins and ends by royal order, and each holder's order must be read. It dates nobody.

claims.text: Article 11: the Chairman, the members and the Secretary-General take the prescribed oath before the King before they begin their work in the Council.
claims.locator: Article 11
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. It separates appointment from the oath and from the start of work but gives no dates; an oath is never read as a stated day of taking office.

claims.text: Article 13: the Council's term is four Hijri years from the date specified in the royal order forming it; a new council is formed at least two months before its predecessor's term ends, the old council continues if the term ends first, and at least half the members of a new council must be new.
claims.locator: Article 13
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. Each term's start depends on the date stated in its forming order; no term end is computed from it.

sources.title: King Fahd Delegates Crown Prince to Undertake State's Affairs (January 1, 1996), Internet Archive capture 20000930104650
sources.publisher: Royal Embassy of Saudi Arabia, Washington, Information Office (saudiembassy.net)

claims.text: Release dated January 1, 1996 on the Royal Embassy's January 1996 page: 'The Custodian of The Two Holy Mosques King Fahd Bin Abdulaziz directed the following Royal Decree to Crown Prince His Royal Highness Prince Abdullah Bin Abdulziz, the deputy Premier and head of the National Guard'.
claims.locator: January 1996 page; item 'KING FAHD DELEGATES CROWN PRINCE TO UNDERTAKE STATE'S AFFAIRS', date line and first sentence
claims.uncertainty: An English release of the Royal Embassy, not the Arabic decree. It attests his title on this day only: it gives no accession date and does not change his CLAUDE-C01-06 holder, whose attested_on (1990-08-08) rests on a foreign record.

claims.text: The same release addresses the decree to 'Crown Prince His Royal Highness Prince Abdullah Bin Abdulziz, the deputy Premier and head of the National Guard' and prints his reply as from 'the Crown Prince, His Royal Highness Prince Abdullah Bin Abdul Aziz'.
claims.locator: January 1996 page; same item, first and second paragraphs
claims.uncertainty: A point observation that predates his CLAUDE-C01-06 Crown Prince holder's attested_on (2005-08-01), which is kept unchanged; whether the holder should be dated from it is a ruling question. It does not date the start of his crown-princeship. 'Abdulziz' is printed so in the decree sentence.

claims.text: The decree, 'after reviewing article 65 of the basic system of Government', says: 'we hereby delegate your Highness to undertake the affairs of the state while we enjoy rest and recuperation'; the Crown Prince's reply accepts the delegation 'to run the affairs of the state on your behalf'.
claims.locator: January 1996 page; same item, decree text and reply
claims.uncertainty: A delegation of the King's functions for a period of rest: acting service, recorded as a claim only. It is not a vacancy, a transfer of the crown or a boundary of either office. The release prints neither the decree's number nor a Hijri date.

sources.scope_note: The Royal Embassy of Saudi Arabia in Washington (Information Office) filed its January 1996 releases on one page under press_release/96_spa/; an official Saudi government publication in English, not the Arabic decree. Only the 1 January item on the delegation is imported; the page's other items, including the budget session chaired by the Crown Prince that day, are leads.

holder_claims.name: Fahd bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
holder_claims.note: Observed as King on 8 August 1990 in a U.S. official record (SA-EXEC-01). The Royal Court announced his death on 1 August 2005 (26/6/1426 AH).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The 1990 observation is a foreign record; no Saudi 1990 record, 1982 accession or 1996 delegation is sourced, and continuity between 1990 and 2005 is not observed. The death announcement states no day or hour of death, so until is null rather than the announcement date.

holder_claims.name: Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
holder_claims.note: Family pledge as King reported by the Royal Court statement dated 1 August 2005 (SA-EXEC-02). Died at 1 a.m. on Friday 3/4/1436 AH, 23 January 2015, styled King (SA-EXEC-05).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The accession statement gives no separate date for the family pledge, so attested_on is the statement date and from is null. until is the stated day of death. No observation between the two dates is recorded.

holder_claims.name: Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
holder_claims.note: Received the pledge as King under the Basic Law, reported by the Royal Court statement of 23 January 2015 (SA-EXEC-05). Separately observed as King on 27 September 2022 and 13 August 2026.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No coronation, oath, inauguration or effective-date wording is recorded, so from is null. No end date is inferred, and continuity to 7 September 2026 is not established.

holder_claims.name: Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
holder_claims.note: Styled Crown Prince, Deputy Premier and Commander of the National Guard when King Fahd's death was announced on 1 August 2005; the same day's Royal Court statement reports the family pledge to him as King (SA-EXEC-01 and 02).
holder_claims.uncertainty: A point observation: the start of his crown-princeship is outside the sources read. His accession ended it, but the statement gives no separate date for the family pledge, so until is null.

holder_claims.name: Sultan bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
holder_claims.note: Selected Crown Prince by King Abdullah after the family pledge, reported by the Royal Court statement dated 1 August 2005 (SA-EXEC-02). Died at dawn on Saturday 24/11/1432 AH, 22 October 2011, styled Crown Prince (SA-EXEC-03).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The selection has no separate date or time beyond the statement date, so from is null. until is the stated day of death.

roles.title: Chairman of the Shura Council

holder_claims.name: Muhammad bin Ibrahim bin Jubair
holder_claims.note: Styled Chairman of the Shura Council when King Fahd wrote to him on the end of the Council's first term and when he presided over its final meeting, 6 July 1997 (SA-CHR-03); Council records also show him as Chairman at the opening of the first term (1414 AH, SA-CHR-02). Named Chairman again in the forming orders A/72 (1997) and A/80 (2001), he took the oath with each new council (14 July 1997, 4 June 2001) and died in office on 24 January 2002, as the Royal Court announced.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No order of his first appointment was read (Royal Orders A/14 and A/16 of 3/3/1414 AH are cited but unread), so from is null and attested_on is his earliest dated attestation. until is the stated day of death in the Royal Embassy's release of the Royal Court announcement; if that release is not accepted as an official Saudi record, until reverts to null, because the Council's own statements of his death are undated. The 1997 and 2001 designations and extensions are continuations, not new tenures.

holder_claims.name: Saleh bin Abdullah bin Humaid
holder_claims.note: Appointed Chairman with the rank of minister by a royal decree issued on 7 February 2002 (24/11/1422 AH), after Jubair's death. The Council's magazine states that he began work as Chairman on Monday 28/11/1422, 11 February 2002, and he chaired his first session on 12 February 2002 after taking the oath (SA-CHR-03). Last attested as Chairman in this packet on 31 March 2002.
holder_claims.uncertainty: from is the stated day he began work as Chairman; the decree's number and any effective day in it were not read, and the oath is undated. If the Royal Embassy's release of the decree is not accepted as an official Saudi record, attested_on moves to 11 February 2002. until is null: no relief, resignation or death is stated. Royal Order A/13 of 14 February 2009 appoints a successor without relieving him, and on 1 March 2009 he is styled Chairman of the Supreme Judicial Council; neither is used as an end.

holder_claims.name: Abdullah bin Mohammed bin Ibrahim Al Al-Sheikh
holder_claims.note: Relieved as Minister of Justice and appointed Chairman of the Shura Council at ministerial rank by Royal Order A/13 of 19/2/1430 AH (14 February 2009), with effect from 3/3/1430 AH (28 February 2009); took the oath on 1 March 2009 (SA-CHR-04). Named Chairman in each later forming order (A/45 2013, A/54 2016, A/146 2020, A/84 2024) and took the oath with each council (SA-CHR-05 and 06); styled Chairman by SPA on 6 and 7 September 2026 (SA-CHR-10).
holder_claims.uncertainty: from rests on A/13's stated effective day, printed in Hijri only and converted through SPA datelines; if that conversion is not accepted, from reverts to null. until is null: no relief, resignation or death is recorded, and continuity to 7 September 2026 is not established beyond the dated observations. The later forming orders are continuations, not new tenures.

roles.scope_note: CLAUDE-C01-25. One holder per person-tenure in chronological order, each followed by its dated holder observations (claim IDs of forming orders naming him, oaths and in-office attestations). A forming order that names the sitting Chairman again, and any extension or renewal, is a continuation and never a new holder. from and until are given only where a source states the day: a stated effective day (A/13), a stated first day in office (the Council's magazine) and a stated day of death (the Royal Court). Appointment reports and orders without an effective day, oaths, term starts and openings, acting presiding by a Vice Chairman, retrospective statements, calendar equivalences, translations, republications and law texts are claims only and never boundaries; a successor's start is never an end.
